summary: Added src/content/blog/beginner/faint-life-line-meaning.md, item 16 from docs/editorial-backlog.md's Next 25 list (67 -> 68 published blog posts). The article is bounded to a single Benham sentence -- 'The thin line does not mean that the subject is necessarily delicate or sickly, but it shows that he cannot endure as much hardship' -- which was already quotation-marked and live in life-line.md and which this repository's own Batch 2C quotation-verification pass (source-verification-log.md) had already confirmed as a genuine, correctly attributed Benham quotation (one of life-line.md's 10 kept/verified quotations), not one of the corrected ones. The article quotes it character-for-character identical to the existing instance (checked by exact-string grep across both files). Attempts to independently re-verify the quotation against a primary Benham scan directly, and to find additional bounded source material specifically about a faint (not just thin) line, were blocked: WebFetch returned EGRESS_BLOCKED for every primary-text host tried (Internet Archive, chestofbooks.com, iapsop.com, sacred-texts.com). A web search surfaced a longer, unverified version of the passage (an 'overstrain'/'health will surely suffer' extension) generated by the search tool's own summarization rather than retrieved primary text; that extension was explicitly not used anywhere in the article, both because it does not meet this repository's verification standard and because the health-outcome framing is exactly what the task packet prohibits. Per the packet's instruction to narrow scope when evidence supports only a bounded claim, the article restricts itself to the one sentence already verified in this repository's own record. It keeps faintness observationally comparative (no fixed depth threshold or population average), explicitly distinguishes faintness from length (with a pointer to short-life-line-meaning.md) and from a genuine break, introduces no stronger-with-degree rule, makes no combination reading with length/breaks/forks/double lines/endpoints/mounts/hand shape/texture, and excludes medical, lifespan, danger, and deterministic health/vitality claims directly on the strength of Benham's own quoted denial ('does not mean... delicate or sickly'). Added one reciprocal link from life-line.md's existing Explore further list; no other wording in that pillar file was reopened.

source_preflight.notes: Full claim-by-claim disposition, including the network-access constraint that narrowed the evidence boundary to a single already-verified sentence, is recorded in docs/source-verification-log.md under 'Faint Life Line Meaning companion article'. The quotation is not new evidence acquisition -- it reuses a sentence this repository's own Batch 2C corpus-match pass already verified and that remains live in life-line.md -- so the preflight consisted of confirming exact quotation fidelity against that existing verified instance and confirming no interpretive claim in the new article goes beyond what the quoted sentence itself states. No prevalence/consensus, precision/degree, vague-authority, or health/vitality/lifespan claim was introduced; faintness is kept separate from length, breaks, forks, double lines, endpoints, mounts, and hand shape throughout; observation, Benham's named historical interpretation, and Palmistry Path's own editorial/safety policy are in distinguishable sections.
